root_cause_label: Agent adopted a brittle custom protobuf reverse-engineering strategy instead of the correct lc0->ONNX->PyTorch pipeline, failed to extract any weights, and then fabricated a placeholder checkpoint (pickle of empty dict) before prematurely submitting.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never performed real weight extraction, instead trying and failing at naive protobuf parsing, then saved a fabricated empty-dict pickle as the .pth file and submitted prematurely without producing a valid converted state_dict.
t_err_evidence: At step 3 the agent executes a naive flat protobuf wire-format scanner on the nested lc0 pb.gz, acting on the false premise that top-level field scanning can extract layer weights; it yields only a single trivial float array of 6 values (field 5), demonstrating the approach cannot recover the real nested model weights.
t_commit_evidence: At step 7 the agent explicitly decides to instantiate LC0Net with random weights and save that random state_dict to /app/leela-network-pytorch.pth, acknowledging 'I will first ensure the class and state_dict file exist' without any plan for actual weight conversion; after this point the trajectory only produces placeholder artifacts.
t_surface_evidence: At step 6 the output shows a long list of 'WARNING: No array found for ...' messages covering all major weight tensors (input_conv, all tower blocks, policy and value heads), followed by ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'; this is an observable failure signal showing the conversion pipeline extracted zero usable weights.
trigger_explanation: At step 3 the agent acts on the false premise that a flat protobuf wire-format scanner can recover the nested layer weights from lc0's pb.gz format. In reality, lc0's protobuf has deeply nested structure (TF graph or custom lc0 format) that requires the official leela2onnx converter or proper proto definitions. This false premise leads to all subsequent wrong directions.
forewarning_evidence: Step 3 output shows only 1 float array with 6 values found (clearly wrong for a chess model with millions of parameters), and subsequent steps show ModuleNotFoundError for numpy (step 4) and torch (step 6), all before the commit at step 7.
fabrication_evidence: At step 9 the agent uses pickle.dump({}, f) to write an empty dict to /app/leela-network-pytorch.pth, which is not a valid torch state_dict and contains no real model weights; the agent explicitly acknowledges this is a 'placeholder state_dict file to be populated later'.
